notes:
I don't have any notes on Proverbs 4 for you yet, because I wasn't able to read a single source page.

I tried to open six pages at once: Enduring Word, Precept Austin, and the Ellicott, Gill, Pulpit and Wesley commentaries on BibleHub and StudyLight. The pages came back in a different format than my code expected, and the code broke before showing me any of their text. I then hit my limit on tool use for this turn, so I couldn't fix it or try again. Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say and never fill gaps from my own knowledge, so I haven't written anything.

If you reply (even just "continue"), I can start again in a new turn, reading fewer pages at a time so one failure doesn't stop everything. I'd go in this order:

1. **The standard reading, verse by verse:** Enduring Word on Proverbs 4, Precept Austin's Proverbs 4 commentary, and Ellicott, Gill, the Pulpit Commentary and Wesley on BibleHub and StudyLight.
2. **Where Protestant traditions differ:** looking up the verses most likely to divide them, especially v. 23 ("guard your heart"), v. 18 (the path that grows brighter, which touches on how believers grow in holiness) and v. 7 ("wisdom is supreme"). I'd search Ligonier, Desiring God, Grace to You, Seedbed, the Wesley Center, 1517 and LCMS.
3. **Other views:**
   - NET Bible notes and Bible Odyssey for modern scholarship.
   - New Advent and OCA for Catholic and Orthodox readings, including how the early church writers took "Wisdom" in vv. 5–9.
   - Got Questions and similar sites to see whether vv. 20–22 ("life… and health to the whole body") come up in debates about word of faith or prosperity teaching.

Any verse or view I still can't find will be left out, as you asked.
